subject: general-mathematics
title: Probability
summary: How likely something is, from coins and dice to picking from a bag, and combined events.

lesson.text: Probability measures how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). When all outcomes are equally likely: P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes.

lesson.title: A fair die is thrown. Find P(even number).

lesson.text: P(not A) = 1 − P(A). The chance of not throwing a 5 is 1 − 1/6 = 5/6.

lesson.title: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls. One is picked.

items: Independent events, "A and B": multiply. P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
Events that can't both happen, "A or B": add. P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

lesson.title: Two fair coins are tossed. Find P(two heads).
steps: P(head) = 1/2 for each coin, and the coins don't affect each other.
Check by listing: HH, HT, TH, TT. One out of four is HH.

lesson.text: Remember: "and" usually means multiply, "or" usually means add. And no probability can be more than 1.

questions.prompt: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Greater than 4: 5 and 6, so 2 outcomes out of 6. 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 green and 6 yellow sweets. One is picked at random. What is P(green)?
questions.explanation: Total = 4 + 6 = 10. P(green) = 4/10 = 2/5. 4/6 divides by the yellow sweets instead of the total.

questions.prompt: A card is drawn from a pack of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that it is a king?
The probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.3. What is the probability that it does not rain?
A fair coin is tossed and a fair die is thrown. What is P(head and a 6)?
questions.explanation: The events are independent, so multiply: 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12. Adding (1/2 + 1/6 = 2/3) is for "or", not "and".
